Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star, then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud had an exceptional fourth quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

One of our key competitive advantages in the cloud computing space is our robust data breach prevention and incident response measures. In an industry dominated by hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, which hold over 65% market share per Synergy Research Group's Q4 2023 report—though our metrics reflect updates into 2024—trust remains the ultimate currency. A single breach can wipe out billions in enterprise annual recurring revenue, as seen with the $4.45 billion in direct costs from the 2023 MOVEit incident across supply chains, according to IBM's Cost of a Data Breach Report. At AetherCloud, we've fortified our defenses and turned security into a revenue driver, powering our 28% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.8 billion in the quarter and keeping churn below 1% in our multi-tenant SaaS workloads.

Our prevention strategy rests on zero-trust architecture across more than 150 global regions managing 50 zettabytes of customer data. We allocated $285 million in FY24, a 32% increase year-over-year and 10% of total operating expenses, to next-generation tools that blocked 1.47 billion malicious login attempts and 2.3 million DDoS attacks—a 45% rise from FY23 amid escalating state-sponsored threats to cloud providers.

Key elements include our AI- and ML-driven threat hunting via the SentinelAI platform, leveraging custom-trained models on NVIDIA A100 GPUs for behavioral analytics that spot anomalies 300 milliseconds faster than traditional SIEM systems. This cut false positives by 62%, dropping quarterly alerts from 15 million to 5.7 million, freeing our 850-person SecOps team for genuine threats. We enforce end-to-end AES-256 encryption for all data at rest and in transit with customer-managed keys through our key management service, at FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance—adoption among Fortune 500 customers hit 78%, up from 52% last year. Following SolarWinds, we've hardened our supply chain with SBOM scanning for all third-party container images in Kubernetes environments, rejecting 18,000 vulnerable ones in Q4 via integrations with Aqua Security and Sysdig.

These efforts deliver regionally. In EMEA, amid GDPR fines averaging €2.5 million per violation per 2023 ENISA data, our DPO-certified controls drove 42% growth in regulated workloads like banking, with zero reportable incidents. In APAC, complying with data sovereignty in places like India's PDPB and Indonesia, we've localized 15 edge data centers, shrinking latency-related attack surfaces by 35% and clinching deals with telcos like Singtel.

On incident response, our playbook excels with mean time to detect at 17 minutes and mean time to respond at 2.8 hours in FY24—improved 72% and 81% year-over-year, surpassing Gartner's Magic Quadrant leaders averaging 45 minutes for detection. Our Global IR Center in Ashburn, Virginia, plus hubs in Singapore and Frankfurt, runs 24/7 with 120 specialists holding GIAC and CISSP certifications. Quarterly Chaos Engineering simulations using Gremlin test our 99.999% SLA for control plane services.

Partnerships boost this: Managed detection and response with CrowdStrike Falcon and Palo Alto Networks Cortex XDR spans 95% of our customer base, auto-quarantining 247 potential incidents in Q4—none became breaches. For ransomware, up 37% year-over-year per Sophos 2023 data, our immutable backups on ObjectStore, S3-compatible with air-gapped replication, restored 100% of simulated attacks in under an hour.

This resilience boosts stickiness: Security upsells added $156 million to ARR, with 92% renewal in high-compliance sectors like healthcare under HIPAA and HITECH, topping Azure's 88% in peers.

Geopolitically tailored, in the US our FedRAMP High GovCloud blocked 420 million adversarial probes in Q4, securing $420 million in federal contracts. China's MLPS 2.0 drove a 25% capex bump in Shanghai for tenant isolation. Cloud security spend is set to reach $125 billion by 2027 at 15.4% CAGR per IDC, spurred by AI—our GPU inference services countered a 55% attack surface growth with Falco eBPF probes.

Looking ahead, Q1 FY25 brings quantum-resistant post-quantum cryptography using NIST's Kyber algorithm against harvest-now-decrypt-later risks, plus confidential computing with Intel SGX and AMD SEV-SNP, piloted with 12 betas for homomorphic encryption.

The return is stark: Each dollar in security yields $4.20 in retained ARR per our models, versus $9.44 million average breach costs for clouds per IBM. This fortifies us for 35% growth in sovereign cloud amid 65% hybrid/multi-cloud enterprise adoption per Flexera 2023.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in the fourth quarter. Revenue grew by 28% year-over-year to $2.8 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 75%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 32%.

Turning to our outlook on macroeconomic factors and their expected impact through FY25, cloud computing remains resilient yet exposed to high interest rates, moderating inflation, and uneven global growth. Our subscription model, now 92% of total remaining performance obligations, offers strong insulation. Headline inflation cooled to 3% in the US and Eurozone per recent CPI, but core at 4-5% sustains Fed funds at 5.25-5.50%. We model two 25 basis point cuts by year-end, terminal at 4% by mid-2026. Higher rates squeeze IT budgets, especially capex, but favor our opex cloud elasticity—workload migrations to our platform rose 15% year-over-year, aligning with AWS and Azure hybrid accelerations.

Demand holds firm: FY25 revenue growth projected at 19-22%, topping our 28% 10-year CAGR, led by AI/ML. Hyperscalers ramp gen AI inference 35-40% year-over-year, training clusters using 2-3x GPU capacity. Our NVIDIA H100 and A100 reservations are 95% utilized; early Blackwell access sets $5-7 billion AI run-rate by FY26, like Google Cloud's 29% Vertex growth. Enterprises soften—SMB expansions delayed 10-15% quarter-over-quarter, mid-market RPO down 5% from hiring pauses—but RPO grew 26% to $145 billion, visible through H2 FY26.

North America, 55% of revenue, grows 22% on datacenter builds and CHIPS Act. Fifteen new edge zones in 2025 aid AI for autos and medicine. Europe, 25%, lags at 14-16% from 20% energy hikes post-Ukraine, but sovereign clouds yield $2.3 billion in commitments like Oracle's OCI. Forex subtracts 1.5%. APAC, 18%, expands 25-28% on China's RMB 10T stimulus, 40% GPU attach in Shanghai/Singapore; India's Digital India ups public deals 30%. Latin America, 2%, grows 32% on Brazil hyperscale.

Costs manageable: Power up 15-20%, 25% of datacenter opex; PUE 1.18, capex $28-32 billion or 13-14% of revenue for 20 AZs, liquid cooling for 100kW AI racks. GPU delays 6-9 months hedged 80% via $1.2 billion TSMC/Samsung contracts; server inflation 8% offset by 12% ARM Graviton efficiencies, 35% of new AI at 40% lower TCO.

Mitigations: AI Accelerate bundles discount inference 20-30% for $10 million-plus ARR, targeting 15% uptake like Azure OpenAI. FinOps right-sized 18% idle resources for 2,500 customers, $1.5 billion savings, 5-7% NRR boost. Ørsted 5GW renewables by 2028 cut volatility 30%, meeting 40% ESG RFPs.

Downside—zero cuts, 1% GDP—17% revenue, 20% RPO. Upside—easing, AI surge—25%+. FCF 25-28% margins fund $15 billion buybacks/dividends. Cloud tailwinds like AI, edge, sovereignty ensure outperformance.

Now, I'll hand it over to Taylor Kim for a technical update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new SentinelAI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

One of our standout differentiators is network performance and reliability. In an industry led by AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, our global backbone with 450+ PoPs and 200+ terabits per second inter-data-center capacity outperforms benchmarks, driving 28% year-over-year growth in IaaS and PaaS.

Q4 averaged 99.999% availability—five nines, under 5.26 minutes monthly downtime—up 15 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 99.998%, 0.02 points year-over-year, exceeding 99.99% SLA and avoiding $12 million credits. G2 Fall 2024 scores us 94/100 reliability, topping AWS's 92.

MTBF for routers/switches: 1.2 million hours, up 18% year-over-year via refreshes. MTTR for P1: 14.2 minutes, half Gartner's 28-minute Tier 1 average. Packet loss: 0.0008% globally, down 25% quarter-over-quarter despite EMEA DDoS spikes.

Latency excels for AI: intra-region 7.8 ms, beating 10 ms target, down 22% year-over-year. Inter-region 42 ms P99 via AetherExpress anycast, 24% faster than Azure's 55 ms, aiding trading/gaming.

Throughput: peak 98.5 Tbps egress, 2.1 Tbps average per PoP, up 35% year-over-year with NVMe-oF/RoCEv2. Customers like FinTech PayNova scaled to 1.6 Tbps seamlessly.

Americas (52% traffic): 99.9995%, 6.2 ms intra, zero P1 over 5 minutes despite Hurricane Milton; edge caching handled 40% extra.

APAC (42% revenue growth): 99.998%, 8.4 ms intra; Equinix 5G backhaul cut mobile edge 30%. India BGP issues hit 68 ms P99, fixed with 12 new peers for 20% drop Q1 2025.

EMEA: 99.9992%, 9.1 ms intra; QUIC kept Dublin-Frankfurt at 38 ms vs. GCP 46 ms.

Initiatives: AetherShield AI NOC predicts 87% anomalies 30 minutes ahead using 10 petabytes daily eBPF telemetry. Nexus Fabric SDN enables 40% faster 100 edge rollouts. 100% renewable undersea cables like AetherLink (22 Tbps) cut latency 15%, carbon 28%; 95% renewable network by 2026.

NPS 78 from 69, gross retention 94%, $2.1 billion contracts with SLAs like WayForge's $450 million sub-5 ms edge AI. Churn 0.3% vs. 2-3% industry.

FY25: 99.9997% availability, sub-7 ms intra. Catalysts: Ericsson 5G slicing, quantum-safe crypto, $1.5 billion photonics CapEx. IDC's $250 billion cloud network by 2027 favors our 15-18% high-margin share.

I'll now pass it to Morgan Patel for a product roadmap update.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. This quarter, we launched NexAI, a game-changing solution for enterprise AI workloads. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Our enterprise customer momentum stands out, driving record net new ACV of $1.2 billion, up 45% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. We added 62 logos over $1 million ACV—our best quarter—and closed 18 deals over $10 million TCV, averaging $22 million, eight multi-year over $50 million including two seven-figure NexAI expansions.

Highlights: Financials—$85 million five-year with GlobalBank Holdings, top-10 bank, modernizing core banking on Kubernetes, NexEdge AI fraud detection, 35% TCO savings; 40% utilization in 60 days.

Manufacturing—$62 million with AutoForge Industries EV batteries: serverless IoT from 500,000 sensors, Databricks data lakes, NexML maintenance; $5 million pilot expanded 12x, displacing VMware/competitors.

Healthcare—$45 million MediCore: HIPAA sovereign region for federated learning across 200 hospitals.

Americas 58% net new ACV at $700 million on VMware migrations (20+ displacements). EMEA up 55% to $320 million on GDPR sovereignty. APAC 70% to $180 million via Tokyo-2/Sydney-3 Graviton4, 50% egress cuts for NTT Docomo-like.

Tailwinds: 65% large deals with NexAI (3x denser inference than AWS Inferentia); VMware flight (15 $30 million deals); sustainability (28% Scope 3 cuts for CSRD).

NRR 128%, expansions 5:1 churn; RPO up 42% to $18.5 billion, 70% deployable in 12 months. Pipeline $4.2 billion, up 50%, 55% AI/edge.

This flywheel redefines AI-era multi-workload cloud.

Now, back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Morgan. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

Before questions, a note on currency fluctuations' revenue impact. As a global provider with over 55% of our $26.4 billion full-year revenue international across IaaS, PaaS, SaaS—from GPU clusters to hybrid edge—volatility affects us, but diversification helps.

Full-year FX headwinds: $450 million or 1.7%, making growth 28% FX-neutral vs. reported 26%. Q4: $180 million or 2.8% of $6.5 billion, vs. Q4 2023 $120 million tailwind, from USD strength vs. EM currencies.

EMEA (28%, $7.4 billion): euro -6%, GBP -4%, $210 million drag; constant-currency 32% on sovereign like Germany/France GDPR migrations.

APAC (22%, $5.8 billion): AUD steady for 15% ANZ 5G; yen -12%, won -8%, $140 million; 30% constant-currency on Inferentia AI.

LATAM (8%, $2.1 billion): real -11%, peso volatility, $70 million; 25% constant-currency on Mexico/Brazil DR.

North America (42%): 24% growth insulated.

DXY up 7% on Fed vs. global cuts; prior 2022 $320 million headwind, 2023 tailwind. FY25: $100-150 million modeled, up to $250 million on EM risks.

Mitigations: 75% FX forwards (euro/yen/real), up from 60%; 40% local billing like Microsoft. Dynamic pricing, local DCs (São Paulo/Jakarta) offset. Nexara Arc interoperability, AutoScale optimization. Monthly Monte Carlo informs Q1 $6.7-6.9 billion, 27-29% FX-neutral.

RPO up 35% to $45 billion constant-currency. Our treasury positions us strongly.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Ross:
Thanks for the details, team. On the security front, could you expand on the quantum-resistant rollout and its timeline for broader adoption?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Mike. As we outlined, Q1 FY25 sees post-quantum cryptography via NIST's Kyber rolling out across key services, addressing harvest-now-decrypt-later risks. We've piloted confidential computing with SGX and SEV-SNP successfully, and expect 20-25% adoption in high-security verticals like finance by year-end, enhancing our moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Given the macro outlook, how firm is FY25 guidance, especially with potential rate paths?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. Our 19-22% revenue guide assumes base macro with two cuts, but FCF margins at 25-28% provide buffer. Upside from AI could push 25%, downside 17% in recession—RPO visibility to H2 FY26 keeps us confident.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Appreciate it. Taylor, on APAC network latency challenges in India, what’s the fix and impact on growth there?

Taylor Kim:
Good one, Raj. BGP peering disputes temporarily pushed P99 to 68 ms, but 12 new Mumbai/Chennai sessions will drop it 20% by Q1 2025. APAC growth stays 25-28%, with Equinix and local builds ensuring edge AI competitiveness.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in AetherCloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
